reviewer: Codex subagent; same model family; context isolated, filesystem access not enforced

scope.method: Python zipfile direct reads; independently recomputed FASTA IDs, lengths, interval character counts, annotation ID joins and coverage, and hints byte/feature counts.
scope.schema_usage: The seven model-output fields in each answer use the supplied schema. rationale and uncertainty are review metadata, not model-output schema fields.

limitations: This is an AI review by a Codex subagent of the same model family, not a human reviewer or an independent domain expert.

Context isolation is procedural: only the delegated review instructions and permitted packet materials were used. Filesystem access was not restricted to the archive; default executor startup failed, so authorized commands ran with require_escalated.
No repository source, other questions, expected.json, meta.json, mapping, prior reports, parent analysis, API keys, external model APIs, or external sources were read.
Conclusions apply only to the declared windows, 32-protein subset, or input file; they do not assess whole-genome quality or species-wide baselines.
Upstream commands, databases and consumption logs are absent. Historical execution and exact upstream causes cannot be established where those records are needed.

R001.action: Allow this window to proceed under the stated consumer contract; retain the ID/length and interval checks.
R001.rationale: The generated delivery satisfies the declared ID/length and lowercase-interval requirements. N in the locating reference is not a delivery defect under its expressly limited role.
R001.uncertainty: Low uncertainty for the stated contract. No independent original-source checksum is supplied, so exact nucleotide provenance beyond the visible interval content is not separately established; genome-wide masking, assembly completeness and library versions are outside scope.

evidence.observation: The complete review set contains 32 proteins; exact first-token query joining and one row per query are required; any 1 in the seven -Annotated columns counts as annotated; required coverage is at least 80%.
The object is an already generated table; no previously accepted version, database, commands, search output or execution log is supplied.
The FASTA has 32 distinct first-token IDs from g1.t1 through g32.t1; all exactly match one row in annotation.tsv.
g1.t1 has 1 in all seven -Annotated columns.
g2.t1 has 1 in all seven -Annotated columns; all remaining 30 query rows have 0 in every -Annotated column.
Reported 6.25% agrees with independent recomputation: 2 annotated proteins / 32 complete queries = 6.25%, below the 80% contract.

R002.action: Withdraw the current table from downstream summary. Obtain the annotation commands, database/version and search/parser logs, trace the unannotated records, repair or rerun as supported by that evidence, then recheck exact ID joins, one row per query and coverage of at least 80% before replacement delivery. No accepted prior table is available to restore.
R002.rationale: The generated table fails a concrete delivery threshold even though ID joins and row cardinality pass. rollback means withdrawing and repairing/rebuilding this unreliable delivery, not claiming that an accepted older version exists. Low coverage alone does not establish low upstream annotation quality or a specific command/database error.
R002.uncertainty: The coverage failure is certain. Its upstream cause is undetermined: true absence of hits, failed searches, filtering or output parsing are possible, but none is proven by the provided materials. Those execution records are needed before assigning a specific cause.

R003.action: Do not start with the current input. Generate or supply a valid hints.gff containing at least one consumer-readable intron feature, then verify this required input before starting; investigate the evidence-generation/export step if the expected hints are missing.
R003.rationale: An empty required input fails the declared startup contract. Since this is preparation rather than a completed delivery, block is appropriate. There is no basis to infer that a past annotation job ignored RNA evidence or to roll back an unseen result.
R003.uncertainty: The current missing-input condition is certain. Why the file is empty and whether any historical workflow used RNA remain unconfirmed; evidence-generation records and actual job consumption logs would be needed for those claims.

evidence.observation: sequence.fa is the already generated delivery; reference.fa is only an ID/length locating file and not an accepted prior delivery.
The declared regions must retain lowercase acgt and base information; replacing these intervals with N is forbidden.
Required lowercase interval is NC_003070.9:1..115.

Independent counts show the three required intervals contain respectively 115, 32 and 33 N, zero lowercase acgt: all 180 required positions lost the required base representation. The delivered record length is still 4096.
Reference ID NC_003070.9 and length 4096 match the delivery; matching ID/length does not satisfy the separate lowercase/base-retention contract.

R004.action: Withdraw the current incompatible sequence delivery. Rebuild from a source preserving the original acgt bases using the required lowercase representation, then check ID/length and every declared closed interval before reissuing. Do not treat the locating reference as an accepted delivery version.
R004.rationale: The generated sequence demonstrably uses N in every interval where lowercase bases are required, so its masking representation violates the consumer contract. The observed mode error supports masking_mode_error at the delivery level; a specific upstream tool invocation is not established.
R004.uncertainty: Low uncertainty about the delivery defect and required withdrawal. The responsible command, parameter, script or earlier transformation cannot be identified without generation records; the visible reference role does not establish an accepted rollback target.
